newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong forecasts record tourism in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong forecasts record tourism in 1997.

text.p: Hong Kong's top finance official forecast on Saturday that a record number of tourists would visit the colony in 1997, the year it returns to China.
Financial Secretary Sir Donald Tsang said a total of 12 million tourists, double the British territory's population, were expected to visit this year.
"For this year, we expect the number of overseas visitors to surge to a record high of over 12 million," Tsang said in a speech marking the 40th anniversary of the Hong Kong Tourist Association.
In 1996, 11.7 million tourists came, nearly a 15 percent increase over 1995's numbers
Speaking 10 days before Hong Kong returns to China, Tsang said the colony ranked eighth in the world in terms of revenue generated by tourists.
"Hong Kong is now the most popular tourist destination in the region," he said.
